transcript:
Header: 2026-12-13 10:00 PST | Duration: 1h15m | Attendees: Liam, Sofia, Marco, Harper, Aurelia, Priya

Summary: Quick sync to align Q1 roadmap priorities and confirm launch readiness checklist for the Redwood Optimize v1 rollout; review recent latency incident and confirm canary + metrics for go/no-go.

Topics: Roadmap priorities; Launch gating criteria; Incident review (11/30 latency spike); Canary plan; Performance benchmarks; QA/beta schedule.

00:00:05 Liam Chen: alright, uh, thanks everyone for joining, let's kick off, quick agenda — roadmap priorities, launch readi- readiness, incident follow-up, and then action items.
00:00:30 Aurelia Park: yeah, quick thing from product side, execs want a tight definition of the launch gates for Q1, they're looking for 95th perc latency and no regression on quality evals, and clear rollback plan.
00:01:05 Sofia Patel: got it. from eng side, we've been tracking the perf suite, the recent quantized models hit the mem targets but 95th has some outliers when sequence > 1024, likely due to batching behavior.
00:01:40 Marco Diaz: those outliers, I think they're the same pattern we saw in the November run — it's about KV cache pressure and merging batches with cold KV cache misses; the runtime falls back to a slightly slower kernel.
00:02:10 Harper Nguyen: yea and perf traces show spikes aligning with cache misses, also a coupling with small background jobs that steal GPU cycles — should talk about isolation for dedicated pools.
00:02:45 Priya Menon: QA's concerned about flakiness in staging — we've seen intermittent failures during heavy parallel evals; could be rate limit + batch packing interactions.
00:03:10 Liam Chen: okay, so for gating we need to be explicit: 95th latency threshold, failure rate < 0.5% for generation requests on the sample prompts, and a rollback plan that includes traffic cut and model variant fallback. Aurelia, can you draft that?
00:03:35 Aurelia Park: yes I'll draft and include a canary percentage and duration, and the exact eval set we use — also note, we should include a cost threshold, execs asked about unit economics.
00:04:05 Marco Diaz: cost thresholds make sense; but we should be careful — cost impact can be controlled by batching and quantization policies. we should publish recommended config per customer tier.
00:04:40 Sofia Patel: for the canary, Eng suggests 10% traffic for 72 hours, continuous perf logging, and automated rollback if 95th increases by >10% vs baseline.
00:05:05 Harper Nguyen: SRE recommends adding a temporary isolation rule so canary runs in a reserved slot of the GPU pool to avoid noisy neighbor issues. we had a noisy neighbor on 11/30.
00:05:35 Liam Chen: speaking of 11/30, Harper can you summarize the incident? what exactly happened and what's outstanding?
00:05:55 Harper Nguyen: short version — a scheduled background job changed a node's cuda driver during a maintenance window, caused a mis-scheduling that led to several KV cache cold misses, which in turn caused a cascade of longer kernel paths; we saw 2.5x latency increase on some requests for about 20 minutes; automatic fallback didn't trip because the variant detection was too strict.
00:06:35 Marco Diaz: right, and there was also an issue in the routing policy where requests got routed to a cheaper variant that wasn't fully compatible with the cached state — that mismatch is the root cause for some errors.
00:07:00 Sofia Patel: transcription note: when we say KV cache often transcribed as 'K V cash' in some logs; just flagging since some of the firefly exports look messy.
00:07:20 Priya Menon: QA found a gap in the smoke tests — we weren't exercising long-seq cases in the preflight, so the regressions only hit under real loads.
00:07:45 Aurelia Park: ok, so action items from incident: Harper to write postmortem, Marco to add compatibility checks for variants in routing, Sofia to augment smoke tests to include long sequences.
00:08:10 Liam Chen: good. next, roadmap priorities — Aurelia, top 3 items for Q1 from product perspective?
00:08:25 Aurelia Park: 1) Redwood Optimize GA (cost/perf toolkit) launch readiness; 2) Private deployment - simplified VPC onboarding; 3) Observability improvements — token-level breakdown and improved tracing.
00:08:55 Marco Diaz: on private deployment, we need to finalize the KMS integration patterns and also a simplified container image for on-prem customers — that will reduce onboarding time.
00:09:20 Sofia Patel: engineering capacity wise, we have two parallel streams: runtime perf improvements (kernel selection and batching) and infra (deployment templates, KMS). we should prioritize perf improvements that most impact 95th latency.
00:09:50 Liam Chen: do we have benchmarks that map perf work to customer impact? Marco?
00:10:05 Marco Diaz: yes, we've been running microbenchmarks and e2e workloads. the spreadsheet shows quantization gives 30-40% token cost reduction but increases tail latency on certain prompts; continuous batching reduces per-token cost but sometimes increases 95th for single-request spikes. I will share the sheet.
00:10:45 Priya Menon: QA request — can we get a stable test harness snapshot so we can run the same workload on each PR? right now tests drift.
00:11:05 Sofia Patel: good point, we'll pin the harness and docker image tag. Marco will publish the tag after he finishes the perf runs.
00:11:25 Liam Chen: roadmap tradeoffs — we need to decide if Optimize GA includes quantization by default or as an opt-in. Aurelia?
00:11:40 Aurelia Park: execs like default-on for cost reasons, but we should avoid user surprises; propose default-on for >=small and add a prominent note for enterprise/private with guidance.
00:12:05 Marco Diaz: technically default-on is ok if we ship clear guardrails and rollback; but we must add a canary specifically for quantized variants.
00:12:25 Harper Nguyen: and SRE will need automation to detect regressions and optionally route to non-quantized variant if the canary fails.
00:12:40 Liam Chen: sounds good. okay, let's talk launch checklist items briefly — what's the minimum we need for go/no-go?
00:12:55 Aurelia Park: docs: public and internal runbooks, security review complete, compliance checklist (SOC2 scoping), perf baselines, canary success for 72 hours, QA signoff, and runbook for rollback.
00:13:20 Sofia Patel: engineering addendum: infra-as-code templates for private, canary automation, smoke tests passing on staging, perf harness stable.
00:13:40 Marco Diaz: also include benchmark numbers on memory, latency, throughput for common seq lengths — 256, 512, 1024, 2048.
00:13:55 Priya Menon: and a bug threshold: critical/sev1s must be zero, sev2s fewer than 3 for go.
00:14:15 Liam Chen: ok I'll capture that. next topic: canary plan details — who does what?
00:14:30 Sofia Patel: Eng will own the canary automation and rollout policy, SRE will provision reserved pools and logging, QA will own verification and sampling. propose 10% traffic for 72 hours with step-up to 25% if stable.
00:14:55 Harper Nguyen: add health checks for model quality — basic perplexity metrics + prompt-set evals every 15 minutes.
00:15:15 Marco Diaz: and log KV cache hit ratios and kernel path distribution so we can detect cold-cache behavior early.
00:15:40 Aurelia Park: include business metrics too — conversion on sample customers for the pilot.
00:15:55 Liam Chen: Great. Now a quick review of outstanding infra tasks — Sofia?
00:16:05 Sofia Patel: infra task list: container image slimming, KMS integration, reserved pool autoscale config, benchmarking infra for multi-tenant load. we have rough ETA: image slimming 2 weeks, KMS patter 3 weeks, reserved pool config 1 week.
00:16:30 Harper Nguyen: for the reserved pool autoscale, we need to ensure scale-down doesn't evict canary workers; will add a config flag.
00:16:45 Marco Diaz: on benchmarking infra, I need to add quantized model tests and a reproducible load generator; I'm blocked slightly by the perf harness version drift.
00:17:05 Priya Menon: QA will coordinate on the bug bash — propose Dec 21 for an internal sweep.
00:17:25 Liam Chen: ok lock Dec 21 for bug bash. Priya will send calendar invite.
00:17:35 Priya Menon: will do.
00:17:45 Liam Chen: any blockers we didn't capture? Marco?
00:17:55 Marco Diaz: main blocker is the routing compatibility check — if we don't validate variant compatibility, the canary could route to a variant that has subtle differences and break things. I'll implement a quick checker.
00:18:15 Sofia Patel: I'll also make sure smoke tests include compatibility assertions.
00:18:30 Harper Nguyen: SRE will add a temporary driver sanity check in maintenance pipeline to avoid the situation like 11/30 where a stray update caused mis-schedules.
00:18:50 Liam Chen: good. let's do a quick timeline review: final gating doc by Dec 18, performance bench and perf harness pinned by Dec 16, canary run start Dec 21? or later?
00:19:10 Aurelia Park: prefer start Dec 22 after bug bash to ensure we don't have fresh regressions from fixes. so canary Dec 22 for 72 hours.
00:19:30 Sofia Patel: works for eng. we should block capacity in the pool starting Dec 21 to prep.
00:19:45 Harper Nguyen: I'll reserve pool capacity Dec 21.
00:19:55 Liam Chen: perfect. circling back to incident postmortem, Harper can you list immediate mitigations?
00:20:05 Harper Nguyen: immediate: add maintenance driver sanity checks, tweak autoscaler to avoid draining canary nodes, add compatibility validation in routing, and adjust variant detection thresholds so fallback triggers earlier.
00:20:30 Marco Diaz: also clear: add a 'compatibility' unit test for each model variant as part of the CI.
00:20:45 Priya Menon: and we'll add long-seq scenarios in preflight.
00:20:55 Liam Chen: ok. action items recap (verbal): Sofia finalize canary runbook; Harper postmortem; Marco perf tests and variant checks; Priya bug bash; Aurelia gating doc. Anything else?
00:21:20 Aurelia Park: I'll also prepare the executive one-pager for launch economics.
00:21:30 Liam Chen: thanks. any risks we should call out now? Marco?
00:21:35 Marco Diaz: risk: quantization tail latency; mitigation: canary + optional opt-out + routing fallback.
00:21:50 Sofia Patel: risk: noisy neighbor; mitigation: reserved pool + isolation + autoscale tweaks.
00:22:05 Harper Nguyen: risk: last-minute infra change; mitigation: freeze non-critical infra changes during canary window.
00:22:20 Liam Chen: ok. quick note on documentation: Marco please populate perf sheet and include notes on test harness tag; Sofia to update runbooks references.
00:22:40 Marco Diaz: will do.
00:22:50 Priya Menon: QA will run regression suite on the pinned harness and report flakiness rate.
00:23:05 Liam Chen: great. any other items?
00:23:10 Aurelia Park: one more ask: legal wants the SOC2 scoping checklist by Dec 18 too — I'll loop in security.
00:23:30 Sofia Patel: security needs the KMS integration plan; I'll coordinate.
00:23:45 Liam Chen: perfect. last brief: do we want a pre-launch dry-run demo to execs? Aurelia?
00:23:55 Aurelia Park: yes, propose Dec 29 for exec dry-run with pilot metrics and canary summary.
00:24:10 Liam Chen: ok block Dec 29, Aurelia will prep slides.
00:24:20 Marco Diaz: small note — some of the logs from the last incident had the product name transcribed as 'Redcraft' in an internal doc, just watch for typos in the postmortem.
00:24:35 Sophia Patel: (laughs) yep noticed that.
00:24:45 Liam Chen: cool. we'll do a concise recap and then close.
00:24:50 Liam Chen: recap: next steps and owners as in action items; canary start Dec 22 post-bug-bash; postmortem due 12/17; gating doc due 12/18; perf harness pinned 12/16; exec dry-run Dec 29.
00:25:10 Aurelia Park: I'll send invites and the gating template.
00:25:20 Priya Menon: I'll send bug bash invite for Dec 21.
00:25:30 Harper Nguyen: I'll start the postmortem and share initial notes by EOD tomorrow.
00:25:45 Marco Diaz: perf sheet will be in the shared drive by 12/16.
00:25:55 Sofia Patel: and I'll own the canary runbook and reserved pool config.
00:26:10 Liam Chen: thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.
